examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
K-map neighbours differ in exactly one bit, so row/column labels use Gray order. Groups have power-of-two size, can wrap around boundaries and may overlap. A group of 2ᵏ cells eliminates k variables. Essential prime implicants uniquely cover at least one required minterm. Don't-cares can enlarge groups but never need coverage; mandatory zero cells cannot be included in an SOP group.

**Key relationship:** A group of 2ᵏ cells eliminates k variables

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Place values using Gray ordering.
2. Choose large valid groups covering every one.
3. Retain essential groups and verify forbidden zeros.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Label both axes in Gray-code order and allow wraparound adjacency. Form power-of-two rectangular groups of 1s for SOP or 0s for POS. A group may overlap another; diagonal cells are not adjacent. Identify essential prime implicants first and then cover any remaining minterms without covering a mandatory zero.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
F(A,B,C,D)=Σm(0,1,2,3,8,9,10,11). How many literals are needed in its minimum SOP?

**Answer: 1.** All eight minterms have B=0 and allow either value of A,C,D. They form an eight-cell group, so F=¬B. Its minimum expression contains one literal.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Use don’t-cares only to improve a chosen group; covering every don’t-care is unnecessary. Do not invent don’t-cares for unspecified minterms.

Diagonal cells are not adjacent unless they are also neighbors through valid edge wrapping.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

A group of four cells in a four-variable K-map yields a product with how many literals?

- **A.** 0
- **B.** 1
- **C.** 2
- **D.** 4

**Answer: C.** Four=2² cells eliminate two of the four variables, leaving two literals.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

Valid SOP K-map group rules include:

- **A.** Power-of-two group sizes
- **B.** Wrapping across opposite boundaries
- **C.** Don't-care cells may be left uncovered
- **D.** Permitting overlap between groups

**Answer: A, B, C, D.** Power-of-two grouping, edge wrapping, optional don't-care coverage and overlapping groups are all valid. Mandatory zeros must still be excluded.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

For F(A,B,C)=Σm(0,1,2,3), how many literals occur in its minimal SOP?



**Answer: 1.** The four minterms cover all B,C values with A=0. Thus F=A′, requiring one literal.

examGuide.title: Work through the supplied PYQs
examGuide.body:
#### GATE 2025 CS2 · Q43 · MSQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/karnaugh-maps?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Karnaugh maps. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. With Gray-code ordering, the four corner 1s group across both wraparound boundaries and give ¬x¬z. The central four 1s give xz. Variables w,y cancel in both groups.
2. Thus F=¬x¬z+xz, option D. Expanding ¬x¬z over both values of w and y yields the four minterms in A.
3. B and C introduce wrong or omit required minterms. Select **A,D**.

#### GATE 2025 CS1 · Q42 · MCQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/karnaugh-maps?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Karnaugh maps. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. On a four-variable K-map, group minterms {0,4,8,12} to get ¬b1¬b0. Group {0,2,8,10} to get ¬b2¬b0.
2. Minterm 11 still needs coverage; pairing {10,11} gives b3¬b2b1. No group can include adjacent zero minterms because there are no don’t-cares.
3. Their sum is **¬b1¬b0+¬b2¬b0+b1¬b2b3, A**. Omitting the last term misses 11.
